## Israel's EU Adequacy Decision Confirmed in 2024

On January 15, 2024, the European Union Commission reconfirmed the adequacy status of Israel in the area of privacy protection, extending the status that was first granted in 2011.

This status confirms that Israel meets the strict standards of the European Union for data privacy, and allows for data transfer from the EU to Israel under the same terms as data transfer within the EU.

### Background and Process

The decision was made after a professional review process that lasted several years, which examined Israeli legislative amendments, case law and the activities of the Israeli Privacy Protection Authority. The decision on Israel's adequacy was issued together with the renewal of recognition for other, previously recognized countries, as per the process mandated by the GDPR, which requires reevaluation every four years.

### Economic Significance

Adequacy status is of great importance to businesses in Israel, because it allows free transfer of personal data from European countries to Israel, without the imposition of additional regulatory or legal requirements, thus reducing costs and minimizing legal risks for Israeli businesses contracting with European partners.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Israel's Privacy Protection Law Amendment 13:

## Amendment 13 Overview

Amendment 13, effective August 14, 2025, introduced significant updates to Israeli data protection law, strengthening the protection of personal data, enhancing data security, and aligning the PPL more closely with global standards like the GDPR.

## Enforcement Powers

The Israeli Privacy Protection Authority (PPA) will gain expanded enforcement powers, including the ability to issue administrative orders, levy significant monetary penalties, and issue cease-and-desist directives. The PPA can conduct routine audits, investigate data breaches, and impose administrative fines on organizations that violate the Israeli data privacy law. Fines may reach millions of shekels, with higher multipliers for large databases or the handling of sensitive information.

## Database Registration Changes

Amendment 13 expands the PPA's enforcement powers, setting financial sanctions for violating the provisions of the PPL and its regulations, updating offenses in relation to databases, and substantive definitions in the PPL, as well as significantly reducing the obligation to register databases.

## Data Protection Officers (DPOs)

If an organization handles a substantial amount of personal data or sensitive information, it must appoint a DPO. The functions of the DPO include overseeing compliance with the PPL and Amendment 13, conducting risk assessments, and ensuring that the company's data processing activities comply with the law. The PPA has announced a temporary grace period regarding the enforcement of that obligation, until October 31, 2025, to allow organizations additional time to prepare.

## Overview

Amendment 13 was adopted in August 2024 and came into effect in mid-August 2025. Amendment 13 marks a pivotal shift by aligning Israel's protection law more closely with global standards, notably the GDPR, by refining definitions, strengthening enforcement, and enhancing data security obligations.

## GDPR Alignment

The amendment aligns Israeli privacy law with global privacy standards, particularly the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), and provides a framework for imposing new administrative fines. The amendment expands key definitions, such as "personal information" and "data processing," aligning more closely with similar provisions in the GDPR.

## Administrative Fines

Administrative fines reach up to NIS 9 million per violation or 5% of annual turnover, and individuals can claim statutory damages of up to NIS 100,000 per person without proving actual harm.

## Privacy Protection Authority Powers

One of the major changes in the amendment is the new powers of enforcement and sanctions granted to the Israeli Privacy Protection Authority (PPA), including significant administrative fines. The PPA can impose hefty fines, order the suspension of data processing and conduct criminal investigations.

## Key Reforms

Key reforms include stronger enforcement mechanisms, new criminal offences, and the introduction of the obligation to appoint data protection officers.

## Draft Guidance Overview

The Israeli Privacy Protection Authority published draft guidance on April 30, 2025, addressing the applicability of Israel's Privacy Protection Law to artificial intelligence (AI) systems, intended to serve as the basis for the Authority's future enforcement activities under Amendment 13, which will come into force in August 2025.

## Key Requirements for Chatbots and Automated Systems

According to the PPA, a person whose personal information is collected and processed by automated system, such as "bots," must be informed of the collection and use, as well as of the manner in which the systems operate, to the extent necessary for receipt of informed consent.

Data subjects must be informed with a clear description of how the AI system functions sufficient to support informed consent, explicit disclosure when interacting with an automated system or a "chatbot", and a detailed explanation of the types and sources of data collected, intended purposes (including training), data recipients and their purposes, and any legal obligations to disclose the data.

## Core Principles

The draft outlines how key privacy law principles apply to AI, such as requiring a legal basis for processing personal data, transparency and disclosures to data subjects, accountability, data security, and data subject rights.

Key requirements include lawful processing bases for all personal data used in AI systems, transparency through clear and informed user consent, and organizations developing or deploying high-risk AI applications are encouraged to appoint dedicated privacy officers and conduct Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs).

The page confirms that **Amendment 13 to Israel's Privacy Protection Law, 1981 took effect on August 14, 2025** and notes it represents "the most significant reform to Israel's privacy regime in decades."

Key points mentioned:
- The PPA published updated guidance and created "a new online information hub to support compliance"
- Organizations must appoint a Data Protection Officer (DPO), with enforcement grace period until **October 31, 2025**
- The PPA warned that "a regulatory warning might precede some sanctions, and others may be levied without warning"

To obtain the exact statutory language, Hebrew definitions (בעל מאגר, מחזיק), and specific obligations you need, you would need to access the actual amended law text or the comprehensive client update referenced in the article.

# Israeli Privacy Protection Authority AI Guidelines – Key Obligations

## Informed Consent & Disclosure Requirements

Organizations must provide data subjects with specific information:

- "the purposes for which the data is being collected"
- "the recipients of the data and the purposes of disclosure"
- "the types of data to be used and their sources"
- "a description of the risks associated with each data processing purpose"
- "how the AI system will process the data"

**Bot Disclosure:** Organizations must disclose "the fact that the data is being collected via an AI-based automated system (bot), if this may significantly affect consent."

## Accountability Measures

Three core practices are emphasized:

1. **Data Protection Officer:** Organizations training AI models are "very likely" to be required to appoint a DPO under Amendment 13.

2. **DPIA Requirement:** Conducting a Data Protection Impact Assessment is described as "the best and recommended way to verify and demonstrate that the use of these systems meets privacy protection requirements."

3. **Generative AI Policy:** Organizations should develop policies addressing which tools are permitted, data types that can be uploaded, prompt retention limits, and employee training on security risks.

## Web Scraping

Scraping personal data without consent "constitutes unlawful privacy infringement," even when publicly posted on social media.

## Controller and Processor Roles

When using the WhatsApp Business API through a Business Solution Provider (BSP), the BSP acts as a Data Processor under Article 28 GDPR, while the business customer remains the Data Controller and retains primary responsibility. For certain processing activities, Meta may act as a processor, and for others (platform security/integrity) potentially as an independent or joint controller.

## Data Processing Agreement (DPA)

Businesses must sign a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) with their provider, a fundamental document that defines roles, responsibilities and the security measures applied when processing end customers' data. The key to compliance is that you sign a contract with the software provider (e.g., a German company), and this provider in turn signs contracts with Meta.

## Legal Basis and Consent Requirements

For sending WhatsApp messages, documented explicit consent under Article 6(1)(a) GDPR is generally required. You may never proactively contact customers without prior opt-in (consent) for outbound messaging. If the customer contacts you first (inbound), this counts as implied consent to begin the conversation, but should be secured through a Double-Opt-In for marketing communications.

## Chatbot and AI Considerations

An integration of GPT models via the WhatsApp Business API, where a Data Processing Agreement and a Zero-Retention Policy exist, can be designed to be GDPR-compliant.

## End-User Data Protection

The API technically has no access to your smartphone's contacts. You only import the data of customers who have explicitly consented (opt-in).

Research complete. Below is a bullet list of falsifiable, sourced claims. **This is research, not legal advice** — for a live product processing real end-user messages, Elia should have an Israeli privacy lawyer confirm the specifics before launch.

## 1. Amendment 13 (תיקון 13) — what changed and when

- **Effective date: 14 August 2025.** Amendment 13 to the Protection of Privacy Law, 1981, entered into force on this date (adopted August 2024, one-year transition). Source: https://iapp.org/news/a/israel-marks-a-new-era-in-privacy-law-amendment-13-ushers-in-sweeping-reform
- **Expanded/modernized definitions.** "Personal information" now covers "any data about an identified or identifiable person (using 'reasonable effort')," and "processing" is "any operation on personal data" — deliberately GDPR-aligned. There is a "new broad perception of sensitive data." Sources: https://bigid.com/blog/what-israel-amendment-13-means-for-businesses-in-2025/ and https://iapp.org/news/a/israel-marks-a-new-era-in-privacy-law-amendment-13-ushers-in-sweeping-reform
- **Consent must be meaningful.** "Consent must be meaningful: informed, voluntary, and in most cases explicit," with "clear opt-in mechanisms" and "full transparency about how data will be used," especially for sensitive data and direct marketing. Source: https://bigid.com/blog/what-israel-amendment-13-means-for-businesses-in-2025/
- **Database registration obligation significantly reduced.** Registration is no longer broadly required; it still applies to databases used for data brokerage / direct-mailing, and controllers must notify the PPA of "any database containing sensitive information on more than 100,000 individuals." Sources: https://bigid.com/blog/what-israel-amendment-13-means-for-businesses-in-2025/ and (reduction of registration obligation) https://www.pearlcohen.com/israel-significant-amendment-to-the-privacy-law-takes-effect/
- **Third-party processor obligation.** Before engaging processors, controllers must "establish robust data processing agreements with clear security obligations" and "continuously monitor vendor compliance." (Israeli law uses the "holder"/מחזיק concept for a party that possesses a database on the owner's behalf; the Data Security Regulations already require a written agreement between owner and holder — Amendment 13 strengthens this.) Source: https://bigid.com/blog/what-israel-amendment-13-means-for-businesses-in-2025/
- **DPO / Privacy Protection Officer now mandatory for certain actors.** Required for large-scale processing of sensitive data, systematic monitoring, public authorities, and data brokers; the officer must be independent and not hold conflicting decision-making authority. Grace period on DPO-appointment enforcement ran until **31 October 2025**. Sources: https://bigid.com/blog/what-israel-amendment-13-means-for-businesses-in-2025/ and https://cookie-script.com/privacy-laws/israel-privacy-protection-law-ppl (grace period)

## 2. GDPR alignment + enforcement/fines

- **Amendment 13 explicitly moves Israeli law closer to GDPR** by refining definitions ("personal information," "data processing"), strengthening enforcement, and enhancing security obligations. Source: https://iapp.org/news/a/israel-marks-a-new-era-in-privacy-law-amendment-13-ushers-in-sweeping-reform
- **PPA gains broad enforcement powers:** administrative orders, monetary sanctions, cease-and-desist directives, suspension of data processing, and criminal investigations. Source: https://iapp.org/news/a/israel-marks-a-new-era-in-privacy-law-amendment-13-ushers-in-sweeping-reform
- **Administrative fines (note: sources disagree on ceilings — flagging uncertainty).** One secondary source cites fines "up to NIS 9 million per violation or 5% of annual turnover," plus statutory damages up to NIS 100,000 per person without proof of harm. Source: search summary citing menoralaw.com / pandectes.io via https://menoralaw.com/israel-data-privacy-law-compliance-2026-guide/. A different source cites "up to ILS 320,000 per violation" for security-requirement breaches. Source: https://bigid.com/blog/what-israel-amendment-13-means-for-businesses-in-2025/. **These figures conflict and should be verified against the statute/PPA before relying on them.**
- **PPA treats its guidelines as effectively binding:** it "will enforce their many quasi-legislative guidelines and directives as if they were binding law," and "a regulatory warning might precede some sanctions, and others may be levied without warning." Source: https://iapp.org/news/a/israel-marks-a-new-era-in-privacy-law-amendment-13-ushers-in-sweeping-reform

## 3. Israel–EU adequacy (cross-border transfer)

- **Confirmed: Israel retains EU adequacy.** On **15 January 2024** the European Commission reconfirmed Israel's adequacy status (first granted 2011), allowing EU/EEA→Israel personal-data transfers without additional safeguards (SCCs, etc.). This was part of the Commission's review of 11 legacy adequacy decisions. Sources: https://www.law.co.il/en/news/2024/01/15/eu-renews-israels-data-protection-adequacy-recognition/ and https://iapp.org/news/a/european-commission-upholds-11-adequacy-decisions
- **Practical implication:** an Israeli business processing EU end-user data can receive it in Israel without an extra transfer mechanism — but adequacy does **not** exempt it from GDPR's substantive obligations when it targets/offers services to EU data subjects.

## 4. GDPR angle for a WhatsApp AI agent (if any end users are in the EU)

- **You (the business) are the data controller; the WhatsApp BSP is a processor under Art. 28.** Meta may act as a processor for some activities and as an independent/joint controller for platform-security activities. Source: https://chatarmin.com/en/blog/is-whatsapp-gdpr-compliant
- **A Data Processing Agreement (DPA) is required.** You must sign a DPA with your provider (which in turn contracts with Meta). WhatsApp publishes Business Data Processing Terms. Sources: https://www.hellomateo.de/en/resources/blog/whatsapp-business-data-processing-agreement and https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/business-data-processing-terms/
- **Lawful basis / consent.** Outbound (business-initiated) messaging generally needs documented explicit opt-in consent under Art. 6(1)(a); inbound (user-initiated) contact counts as implied consent to that conversation, but marketing follow-ups should use double opt-in. Source: https://chatarmin.com/en/blog/is-whatsapp-gdpr-compliant
- **AI-in-the-loop is compatible** where a DPA plus a zero-retention policy are in place. Source: https://qualimero.com/en/blog/whatsapp-business-gdpr-compliant-ai-consultation-guide-2025

## 5. Chatbot / AI-specific guidance under Israeli law (directly relevant to a WhatsApp AI agent)

- **PPA published draft AI guidance on 30 April 2025**, intended as the basis for enforcement under Amendment 13. Source: https://babl.ai/israels-privacy-authority-releases-draft-ai-guidance-for-data-protection-compliance/
- **Bot-disclosure duty:** organizations must disclose "the fact that the data is being collected via an AI-based automated system (bot), if this may significantly affect consent." Source: https://www.gornitzky.com/privacy-in-artificial-intelligence-systems-guidelines-of-the-israeli-privacy-protection-authority/
- **Informed-consent disclosures for AI processing** must include: purposes of collection, recipients and disclosure purposes, types and sources of data, the risks of each processing purpose, and how the AI system processes the data. Source: https://www.gornitzky.com/privacy-in-artificial-intelligence-systems-guidelines-of-the-israeli-privacy-protection-authority/
- **DPIA strongly recommended**, and organizations training AI models are "very likely" required to appoint a DPO under Amendment 13. Source: https://www.gornitzky.com/privacy-in-artificial-intelligence-systems-guidelines-of-the-israeli-privacy-protection-authority/
- **Earlier PPA position (2022):** a person whose personal information is collected/processed by an automated system such as a "bot" must be informed of the collection, the use, and how the system operates, to the extent needed for informed consent. (Primary Library of Congress page returned 403; this is from the search summary of that item — verify directly.) Source: https://www.loc.gov/item/global-legal-monitor/2022-10-20/israel-privacy-protection-authority-announces-scope-of-informed-consent-for-collection-of-personal-information-by-ai/

## Honest uncertainty notes
- **Fine ceilings conflict across sources** (NIS 9M / 5% turnover vs. NIS 320K) — must be checked against the statute and PPA publications before quoting to anyone.
- I could not extract the **exact Hebrew statutory definitions** of בעל מאגר / מחזיק / the sensitive-data list from a primary source; the Tech Policy Institute PDF and the LoC page were not machine-readable/accessible. The controller/holder/consent points above rest on reputable secondary (law-firm and IAPP) summaries.
- The PPA AI guidance is **draft** (April 2025) — it signals enforcement intent but may change.

Most authoritative primary/near-primary sources to hand a lawyer: the IAPP reform overview, the EU adequacy reconfirmation (law.co.il / IAPP), and the PPA draft AI guidance (via Gornitzky/BABL). The definitive text is the Protection of Privacy Law 1981 as amended and the PPA's own hub (referenced but not directly fetched here).
